mainEntity.name: What is affordable crypto PR and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Affordable crypto PR means paying for senior judgment and direct editor access without the overhead of a full agency account team. The right model is a fractional senior operator at $5K–$12K/month or a one-time launch sprint at $15K–$40K. It suits seed-to-Series A Web3 and AI founders who need real tier-1 coverage but cannot justify a $15K–$45K agency retainer.

mainEntity.name: How much does affordable crypto PR actually cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional senior operator retainer runs $5K–$12K/month. A single launch sprint covering positioning, embargo, tier-1 outreach and KOL amplification runs $15K–$40K over four to eight weeks. Wire-blast services cost far less but do not produce earned media. Nano KOLs cost $200–$1.5K per post; micro KOLs $500–$5K. The real cost of cheap PR is the opportunity cost of a news cycle that passes without coverage.

mainEntity.name: What outlets can a small-budget crypto project realistically get into?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a strong news hook and direct editor relationships, even a lean-budget project can land in CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, The Block or Blockworks. Mainstream placements in Forbes, Benzinga or Yahoo Finance require a crossover angle such as AI utility or institutional finance. Regional tier-1 outlets across Korea, Japan, India and Southeast Asia are also reachable. Wire-blast tools reach none of these. Coverage depends on the angle, not the budget size alone.

mainEntity.name: What is the process and how long does affordable crypto PR take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sprint starts with a one-week audit and narrative build, then moves into active pitching in week two. First coverage typically lands in weeks three to four if a real news hook exists. A retainer compounds that base month by month, adding reactive pitching, sustained editor relationships and AI-citation tracking. The highest-leverage window is six to twelve weeks before a major public moment such as a raise, mainnet or TGE.
